approval.condition: Mode 2 only when remediation_enabled=true for the environment and the bucket is allowlisted; otherwise report-only

controls.description: S3 Block Public Access is enabled at the account level and on every bucket, and no bucket policy or ACL grants access to anonymous or all-AWS-users principals.

detection.access_analyzer: external-access findings for S3 buckets (when an analyzer exists)

controls.evaluation_logic: NON_COMPLIANT if any of the four bucket-level Block Public Access settings is false, or if the effective bucket policy or ACL grants Principal "*" or the AllUsers/AuthenticatedUsers groups without a restricting condition. The account-level block is evaluated separately and reported, but never changed by this platform.
evidence_requirements: Config evaluation result (before and after) with timestamps
Allowlist entry identifier that authorised the change

exception_policy.requires: Documented business need (e.g. a public static website), security owner approval, compensating controls (CloudFront OAC), expiry no later than 90 days

controls.rationale: Publicly readable or writable buckets are the most common cause of cloud data exposure. For a financial services company, one public bucket holding customer data is a reportable incident.

remediation.action: Enable all four bucket-level Block Public Access settings (s3:PutBucketPublicAccessBlock)
preconditions: Resource ARN, account and Region match an allowlist entry for SEC-001
Live re-read of the bucket confirms the violation still exists
Bucket is not an evidence, state or log-delivery bucket
remediation.rollback: Restore the previous PublicAccessBlockConfiguration captured before the change

controls.severity_escalation: critical when the bucket policy or ACL actually grants public read/write
controls.title: S3 public access protection

verification.expected: COMPLIANT within one evaluation cycle; all four settings true
verification.procedure: Run the Config rule evaluation again (StartConfigRulesEvaluation) and confirm COMPLIANT, then read GetPublicAccessBlock directly and compare with the expected configuration.

controls.description: Every bucket has default server-side encryption. Buckets classified Confidential or above use SSE-KMS with a customer managed key.
controls.evaluation_logic: NON_COMPLIANT if no default encryption rule exists, or if the bucket is tagged DataClassification in {confidential, restricted} and the default algorithm is not aws:kms. The classification tag only selects the stricter rule; it never relaxes it.
evidence_requirements: GetBucketEncryption output (algorithm and key ARN with the account ID redacted in reports)

exception_policy.requires: Data classification of public or internal and security owner approval; expiry no later than 90 days

controls.mapping_notes: No current CIS AWS Foundations recommendation covers S3 default encryption (CIS removed it after S3 made SSE-S3 the default). PCI DSS 3.5.1 applies only when the bucket stores PAN.
controls.rationale: Encryption at rest limits the impact of media loss and of misconfigured storage access. Since January 2023 S3 applies SSE-S3 to new objects by default, so the control focuses on the stronger SSE-KMS requirement for classified data.

remediation.rationale: Changing encryption keys or algorithms is listed as a prohibited automatic change (encryption keys).

controls.title: S3 default encryption

verification.procedure: Re-evaluate the Config rule; read GetBucketEncryption

controls.description: Buckets holding audit evidence, Terraform state or business records have versioning enabled.
controls.evaluation_logic: NON_COMPLIANT if the versioning status is not Enabled

exception_policy.requires: Bucket holds only reproducible or temporary data; expiry no later than 90 days

controls.mapping_notes: CIS 2.1.2 (v5) / 3.1.2 (v6) MFA Delete depends on versioning, but versioning alone does not meet it, so it is not mapped. PCI 10.3.3 applies only to buckets that store audit logs. SOC 2 A1.2 applies only when the Availability category is in scope.
controls.rationale: Versioning keeps previous object versions after accidental or malicious overwrite or deletion. It is also a prerequisite for S3 Object Lock and MFA Delete.

remediation.rationale: Enabling versioning has a permanent effect (it can be suspended, never removed) and changes storage cost. A human decides.

controls.title: S3 versioning

verification.procedure: Re-evaluate the Config rule; read GetBucketVersioning

controls.description: Bucket policies deny any request made without TLS (aws:SecureTransport = false).
controls.evaluation_logic: NON_COMPLIANT unless the bucket policy has an explicit Deny on s3:* for all principals when aws:SecureTransport is false
evidence_requirements: Bucket policy statement IDs (not full policy) before/after
controls.mapping_notes: PCI DSS 4.2.1 concerns PAN transmitted over open, public networks; it applies only when the bucket holds PAN.
controls.rationale: Stops credentials and data from crossing the network in clear text, including through misconfigured clients.

remediation.rationale: Editing a bucket policy can lock out legitimate principals. Merging a policy automatically is not low risk.

controls.title: S3 HTTPS-only access

verification.procedure: Re-evaluate; attempt an HTTP (non-TLS) GetObject on a test bucket from the validation script and expect AccessDenied

approval.approvers: IAM principals listed in the remediation policy (never the CI roles or the automation role)
approval.timeout: 4h, then the request expires and the finding stays open

controls.description: No security group allows inbound TCP 22 from 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0.

detection.custom_evaluator: src/compliance_evaluator (IPv6 ::/0 and port ranges that include 22)

controls.evaluation_logic: NON_COMPLIANT if any ingress permission with IpProtocol tcp or -1 has a port range that includes 22 and a source of 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0.
evidence_requirements: Offending rule (ID, protocol, port range, CIDR) before the change
Approval record (approver principal, decision, timestamp, comment)
SSM Automation execution ID and step outcomes

exception_policy.requires: Bastion pattern rejected in favour of Session Manager; temporary exception only, max 7 days, named owner

controls.rationale: SSH open to the internet is constantly scanned and brute-forced. Administrative access should go through Session Manager or a restricted CIDR.

remediation.action: Revoke only the offending ingress rule, by security-group-rule ID (ec2:RevokeSecurityGroupIngress)
never: default security groups of existing VPCs
security groups attached to running production workloads
any other rule in the group
preconditions: Resource ARN, account and Region match an allowlist entry for SEC-005
Live DescribeSecurityGroupRules confirms the exact rule still exists
Group is not attached to an ENI outside the project (DescribeNetworkInterfaces)
remediation.rollback: Re-authorise the captured rule (same protocol, ports, CIDR, description). Only on operator request.
remediation.scope: allowlisted project-owned test security groups only

controls.title: Unrestricted SSH ingress

verification.procedure: Re-evaluate the Config rule and re-describe the group; confirm only the offending rule was removed (rule count -1, others unchanged)

approval.approvers: IAM principals listed in the remediation policy

controls.description: No security group allows inbound TCP 3389 from 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0.

detection.custom_evaluator: src/compliance_evaluator (IPv6 ::/0 and port ranges that include 3389)

controls.evaluation_logic: NON_COMPLIANT if any ingress permission (tcp or -1) covering port 3389 has source 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0
controls.rationale: RDP exposed to the internet is a leading ransomware entry point.

remediation.action: Revoke only the offending ingress rule by security-group-rule ID
never: default security groups of existing VPCs
remediation.rollback: Re-authorise the captured rule on operator request
remediation.scope: allowlisted project-owned test security groups only

controls.title: Unrestricted RDP ingress

controls.description: EBS encryption by default is enabled in the Region, and every EBS volume is encrypted.
controls.evaluation_logic: NON_COMPLIANT if a volume has Encrypted=false, or if GetEbsEncryptionByDefault is false in the Region

exception_policy.requires: Volume holds no data (scratch) and is deleted within the exception period (max 30 days)

controls.rationale: Snapshots and volumes of unencrypted disks can be copied or shared without key-level control.

remediation.rationale: Volumes cannot be encrypted in place (snapshot, copy, replace). Turning on encryption by default is an account-wide setting. Both are on the prohibited automatic-change list.

controls.title: Unencrypted EBS volumes

verification.procedure: Re-evaluate after the owner replaces the volume

approval.approvers: IAM principals listed in the remediation policy

controls.description: EC2 instances require IMDSv2 session tokens (HttpTokens=required).
controls.evaluation_logic: NON_COMPLIANT if MetadataOptions.HttpTokens is optional and the endpoint is enabled

exception_policy.requires: Vendor appliance without IMDSv2 support; hop limit 1 and no instance role with sensitive permissions; max 90 days

controls.mapping_notes: No EC2 instance will be deployed without separate approval (prompt section 15). Live demonstration uses synthetic Config events. The SSM runbook is tested offline, and against a real instance only if one is approved.
controls.rationale: IMDSv1 enables SSRF-based theft of instance role credentials.

remediation.action: ec2:ModifyInstanceMetadataOptions HttpTokens=required on the allowlisted instance
preconditions: Owner confirmed the workload's SDKs support IMDSv2 (stated in the approval comment)

controls.title: EC2 IMDSv2 enforcement

controls.description: Every IAM user with a console password has an MFA device.
controls.evaluation_logic: NON_COMPLIANT if the user has a login profile and zero MFA devices
evidence_requirements: user name hashed in public reports
controls.rationale: A password-only console login is one phishing email away from account takeover.

remediation.action: Notify the security operator and the user's owner. Never deactivate users automatically.
remediation.rationale: Disabling a human identity can lock out administrators. IAM administrator permissions are on the prohibited list.

controls.title: IAM users without MFA

verification.procedure: Re-evaluate after the user enrols MFA

controls.description: No customer-managed or inline policy grants Action "*" on Resource "*". Policies that grant service-wide wildcards (for example "s3:*") are reviewed, and external or public access is surfaced by IAM Access Analyzer.

detection.access_analyzer: external access analyzer findings; unused access analyzer is a paid feature and is not used

controls.evaluation_logic: NON_COMPLIANT if an attached, customer-managed policy version has an Allow statement with Action "*" (or "*:*") and Resource "*". Service-level wildcards are flagged for review (medium). AWS managed policies are reported only by attachment.

exception_policy.requires: Break-glass role with MFA, permissions boundary or SCP guardrail, CloudTrail alerting; reviewed every 90 days

controls.rationale: Wildcard administrative policies break least privilege and let one compromised principal take over the account.

remediation.action: Open a review task for the policy owner. Never detach or edit IAM policies automatically.
remediation.rationale: IAM administrator permissions are on the prohibited automatic-change list.

controls.title: Excessively permissive IAM policies

verification.procedure: Re-evaluate after the owner's change; confirm the policy version changed

controls.description: Active IAM user access keys are rotated within 90 days. Keys unused for 45 days are disabled. A user has at most one active key.
controls.evaluation_logic: NON_COMPLIANT if an active key is older than 90 days, unused for 45 days or more, or the user has two active keys

exception_policy.requires: Third-party integration that cannot use roles, key scoped by policy and source-IP condition, max 90 days

controls.rationale: Long-lived static keys leak through code, laptops and CI logs. Workloads should use roles and OIDC (as this project's CI does).

remediation.action: Notify the key owner and the security operator. Never deactivate keys automatically.
remediation.rationale: Deactivating a key in use breaks workloads, and identity changes are on the prohibited list.

controls.title: Long-lived IAM access keys

controls.description: At least one trail records management events in the target Region with logging on, log file validation enabled and delivery succeeding. A StopLogging, DeleteTrail or UpdateTrail call is treated as a security event.
controls.evaluation_logic: NON_COMPLIANT if no trail with IsLogging=true covers the Region, or log file validation is off. MULTI_REGION_CLOUD_TRAIL_ENABLED is reported as informational: the existing trail is single-Region by design because an SCP denies the other US Region (to be confirmed in discovery).
evidence_requirements: CloudTrail event that changed the trail (eventID
controls.rationale: CloudTrail is the audit record every other control and investigation depends on. Turning it off is a classic attacker step.

remediation.action: Page the security operator immediately. Never start, stop, create or modify trails automatically.
remediation.rationale: The trail is a pre-existing, account-level audit service owned by another project.

controls.title: CloudTrail logging status

verification.procedure: GetTrailStatus shows IsLogging=true and a LatestDeliveryTime newer than the event

approval.condition: Mode 2 only with remediation_enabled=true and an allowlist match

controls.description: Taggable resources carry Project, Environment, Owner, ManagedBy and DataClassification.
controls.evaluation_logic: NON_COMPLIANT if any required tag key is missing. Values are validated by the custom evaluator against the allowed-values list in policies/.

exception_policy.requires: Resource type does not support tags, or is AWS-created (service-linked)

controls.mapping_notes: Tagging supports inventory and ownership. The inventory process itself is organisational.
controls.rationale: Tags drive cost allocation, ownership routing of findings and data-classification rules. Tags are an input to decisions, never proof of authorisation (ADR 0006).

remediation.action: Add only the missing tags whose values are stated in the resource's allowlist entry (tag:TagResources). Never overwrite existing values and never invent an Owner.
preconditions: live tag read confirms tags still missing
remediation.rollback: Remove exactly the tag keys that were added (recorded in evidence)

controls.title: Required resource tags

approval.condition: Becomes human_approval when the third precondition fails

controls.description: Every log group has an explicit retention period. Project log groups keep at least the environment's minimum (dev 30 days, prod 365 days).

detection.custom_evaluator: src/compliance_evaluator (log_retention_set; the managed rule treats "Never expire" as COMPLIANT)

controls.evaluation_logic: NON_COMPLIANT if retentionInDays is unset (never expire) or below the environment minimum

exception_policy.requires: Debug log group with no audit value, owner approval; max 90 days

controls.mapping_notes: PCI 10.5.1 asks for 12 months of audit logs (3 immediately available). The dev minimum of 30 days is deliberately below it and is documented as a dev-only deviation.
controls.rationale: "Never expire" log groups grow cost without limit. Retention that is too short destroys evidence. Both are policy violations.

remediation.action: Set retention to the environment's policy value only when the group is currently "never expire" (logs:PutRetentionPolicy)
preconditions: Oldest stored event is newer than the target retention (otherwise data would be deleted, so approval is required)
remediation.rollback: DeleteRetentionPolicy (back to never expire). Data already expired cannot be restored, which is why the third precondition exists.

controls.title: CloudWatch log retention

controls.description: Changes to security-relevant configuration (security groups, bucket policies and public access blocks, IAM policies, CloudTrail, Config, this platform's own resources) made outside the approved pipeline are detected, attributed and escalated. Terraform drift on this platform's stack is detected on a schedule.

detection.custom_evaluator: src/findings_processor change attribution: the principal is compared with the approved change principals (Terraform apply role, remediation automation role). Anything else on a protected resource is "unauthorized" until a human reviews it.
detection.limitation: IAM is a global service whose CloudTrail events reach EventBridge in us-east-1. If an SCP denies us-east-1 (as recorded for this account in Project 2), IAM changes are detected only by the periodic Config evaluation, not in near-real time.
detection.terraform_drift: scheduled drift-detection workflow (read-only plan, exit code 2 = drift)

controls.evaluation_logic: A change event on a monitored resource whose userIdentity.arn (role session issuer) is not in the approved-change-principal list, or whose time is outside an approved change window, produces an unauthorized-change finding. Drift = a non-empty plan for the platform stack.

exception_policy.requires: Emergency change recorded in an incident ticket and reconciled through Terraform within 24h

controls.mapping_notes: CIS 4.x / 5.x monitoring recommendations prescribe CloudWatch metric filters and alarms on a trail's log group. This design uses EventBridge rules on the same CloudTrail events. That meets the detection intent but not the literal audit procedure, so it is "partial". CIS 3.3 / 4.3 (Config enabled in all Regions) cannot be met in a single-Region account.
controls.rationale: Console "quick fixes" and attacker persistence both appear as changes outside change control. Detecting them closes the loop between policy-as-code and the real account.

remediation.action: Investigate and notify. Restoration goes through the reviewed Terraform pipeline (plan, then approved apply), never through automatic revert.
remediation.rationale: An automatic revert of a human change can fight an incident responder.

controls.title: Unauthorized configuration changes

verification.expected: Finding created within 5 minutes; drift workflow exits with drift detected
verification.procedure: Make a controlled console change to a test security group (scenario 15); confirm a finding is created and the drift workflow reports the address
